```{r setup}
# posterior predictive checks (density overlay and mean), by group if given
custom_ppc <- function(fit, group = NULL, ndraws = 100) {
  pal <- scale_fill_viridis_d(begin = 0.3, end = 0.8, alpha = 0.5, option = "mako")
  if (!is.null(group) && group %in% names(fit$data)) {
    p <- list(pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "dens_overlay_grouped", group = group),
              pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "stat_grouped", stat = "mean", group = group))
  } else {
    p <- list(pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "dens_overlay"),
              pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "stat", stat = "mean"))
  }
  plot_grid(plotlist = lapply(p, function(x) x + pal + theme_classic()), ncol = 2)
}

ci <- function(x, digits = 2) paste0(round(median(x), digits), " [95% UI: ",
                                      round(quantile(x, 0.025), digits), "–",
                                      round(quantile(x, 0.975), digits), "]")
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

# Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted}

- Test whether the vocalizations of the focal bellbird are classified more often as the sympatric species it could have imitated than as their allopatric relatives, and more often than the vocalizations of other bellbirds
- Test whether the classifications of the focal bellbird changed over time
- Test whether the imitations and the own song became more similar to real vocalizations of the species and more consistent over time
- Identify the dialects of the focal bellbird's own song and test whether their use and quality changed over time

Classifications come from the cross-validated BirdNET classifiers of the [model fitting](birdnet_model_fitting.qmd) report. The fits are saved in `data/processed/cv_fits/`.

:::

# Cross-validated classifiers

## Design

- All training and test clips were pooled and split into 5 folds grouped by recording (all clips of a recording in the same fold) and stratified by species, seed 123
- For each fold, the classifiers were trained on the other 4 folds (early stopping on a random 20% of the training clips) and classified the held-out fold, so every clip has a prediction from a model that never heard its recording
- Training and classification used a 400–12,000 Hz bandpass
- Hyperparameters were chosen by random search among 30 configurations drawn from the search space of BirdNET-Analyzer's built-in tuner; for each classifier, the simplest configuration within one standard error of the highest out-of-fold macro-averaged AUPRC was selected (rule set before seeing the results, without using the focal bellbird). See the [model fitting](birdnet_model_fitting.qmd) report
- Per-species thresholds maximize F1 on the out-of-fold predictions. A clip is assigned to its highest-confidence species if it reaches that species' threshold, otherwise it is unassigned
- The focal bellbird clips are classified by the 5 fold models of the selected configuration: confidences are averaged across models (ensemble) and the out-of-fold thresholds are applied

```{r selected configurations}
folds <- read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "folds.csv"))
best_cfg <- with(read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "selected_configurations.csv")), setNames(config, model))[models]
data.frame(Classifier = model_labels[models], `Selected configuration` = best_cfg, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
```

## Selected classifiers

Out-of-fold performance by species of the selected configurations.

```{r selected classifiers}
oof <- lapply(setNames(models, models), function(m)
    read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, paste0("oof_predictions_", m, ".csv")), check.names = FALSE))
thr <- lapply(setNames(models, models), function(m) optimal_thresholds(oof[[m]], model_spp[[m]]))
focal_pred <- lapply(setNames(models, models), function(m)
    read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, paste0("focal_predictions_", m, ".csv")), check.names = FALSE))

per_sp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
    r <- cv_metrics(oof[[m]], model_spp[[m]], thr[[m]])$per_species
    data.frame(Classifier = paste0(model_labels[[m]], " (", best_cfg[[m]], ")"), r)
}))
names(per_sp) <- c("Classifier", "Species", "Precision", "Recall", "F1", "AUPRC", "Threshold", "Clips")
kable(per_sp, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

In the sympatric + allopatric classifier the aracaris and the oropendolas are the weakest classes, each confused mostly with its close relative. Out-of-fold confusion matrices (colour: proportion of the clips of each species; numbers: clips):

```{r oof confusion}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5

cm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
    lv <- c(model_spp[[m]], "Unassigned")
    d <- as.data.frame(table(True = factor(oof[[m]]$true, levels = model_spp[[m]]),
                             Predicted = factor(oof[[m]]$predicted, levels = lv)))
    d$Proportion <- d$Freq / ave(d$Freq, d$True, FUN = sum)
    d$Classifier <- paste0(model_labels[[m]], " (", best_cfg[[m]], ")")
    d
}))
cm$Classifier <- factor(cm$Classifier, levels = unique(cm$Classifier))

cm_plot <- function(d, label) {
    ggplot(d, aes(Predicted, True, fill = Proportion)) +
        geom_tile(color = "white") +
        geom_text(aes(label = label, color = Proportion > 0.5), size = 3.5) +
        scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "black"), guide = "none") +
        scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, limits = c(0, 1)) +
        facet_wrap(~ Classifier, scales = "free") +
        labs(x = "Predicted", y = "Vocalizing species") +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "italic"),
              axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), strip.background = element_blank())
}
cm_plot(cm, ifelse(cm$Freq > 0, cm$Freq, ""))
```

Normalized confusion matrices (proportion of the clips of each species; rows sum to 1 and the diagonal is the recall of each species; blank cells: no clips; <0.01: at least one clip but below 0.005):

```{r oof confusion normalized}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5

cm_plot(cm, ifelse(cm$Freq == 0, "", ifelse(cm$Proportion < 0.005, "<0.01", sprintf("%.2f", cm$Proportion))))
```

# Sympatric and allopatric species

Is a heterospecific classification of the focal bellbird more often the sympatric species (a possible model) than its closely related allopatric relative (which it could never have heard)?

Other bellbirds are the out-of-fold predictions of all bellbird clips used to train the classifiers (`r sum(oof$sympatric_and_allopatric$true == "Procnias tricarunculatus")` clips). Each was classified by a model that never heard its recording.

```{r symp allo data}
est <- readRDS("./data/processed/extended_selection_table_sympatric_and_allopatric_species.RDS")
focal_meta <- data.frame(clip = est$sound.files, recording = attr(est, "check.res")$orig.sound.files)
focal_meta <- focal_meta[est$source == "mimic_bellbird", ]

recording_of <- function(clip) sub("\\.wav_[0-9]+$", "", clip)

build <- function(m) {
    fp <- focal_pred[[m]]
    op <- oof[[m]][oof[[m]]$true == "Procnias tricarunculatus", ]
    rbind(data.frame(clip = fp$clip, recording = focal_meta$recording[match(fp$clip, focal_meta$clip)],
                     predicted_sp = fp$predicted, vocalizing_type = "focal"),
          data.frame(clip = op$clip, recording = recording_of(op$clip),
                     predicted_sp = op$predicted, vocalizing_type = "others"))
}

bb_sa <- build("sympatric_and_allopatric")
bb_sa$vocalizing_type <- factor(bb_sa$vocalizing_type, levels = c("others", "focal"))

kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(`Classified as` = bb_sa$predicted_sp, bb_sa$vocalizing_type)))
```

```{r symp allo plot}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

het <- bb_sa[bb_sa$predicted_sp %in% c(heterosp_sympatric, allopatric_spp), ]
het$genus <- factor(sub(" .*", "", het$predicted_sp), levels = c("Pteroglossus", "Psarocolius", "Ramphastos"),
                    labels = c("Aracaris", "Oropendolas", "Toucans"))
het$type <- factor(ifelse(het$predicted_sp %in% allopatric_spp, "Allopatric", "Sympatric"),
                   levels = c("Sympatric", "Allopatric"))
het$bird <- factor(ifelse(het$vocalizing_type == "focal", "Focal bellbird", "Other bellbirds"),
                   levels = c("Other bellbirds", "Focal bellbird"))
n_bird <- table(bb_sa$vocalizing_type)
cnt <- as.data.frame(table(bird = het$bird, genus = het$genus, type = het$type))
cnt$Proportion <- cnt$Freq / as.numeric(n_bird[ifelse(cnt$bird == "Focal bellbird", "focal", "others")])

ggplot(cnt, aes(genus, Proportion, fill = type)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.75) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Freq), position = position_dodge(0.8), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ bird) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Sympatric = "#408AB4", Allopatric = "#7B4F9D")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Vocalizations classified as", fill = NULL) +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank())
```

## Focal bellbird

The probability that a heterospecific classification of the focal bellbird is the sympatric species rather than the allopatric one (0.5 if both were equally likely by chance), with the recording as a random effect.

```{r symp allo focal model}
d1 <- bb_sa[bb_sa$predicted_sp %in% c(heterosp_sympatric, allopatric_spp), ]
d1$mimic_type <- as.integer(d1$predicted_sp %in% heterosp_sympatric)

priors1 <- c(prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = "Intercept"), prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"))

mod1 <- brm(mimic_type ~ 1 + (1 | recording), data = d1[d1$vocalizing_type == "focal", ],
            family = bernoulli(), prior = priors1, chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = cores,
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), seed = 123,
            file = file.path(fit_dir, "sympatric_allopatric_focal"), file_refit = "on_change")
```

```{r mod1 summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| fig-height: 3

extended_summary(mod1, n.posterior = 1000, fill = mako(10)[8], trace.palette = mako,
                 remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE)
```

```{r mod1 ppc}
#| fig-height: 3

custom_ppc(mod1)
```

## Focal vs other bellbirds

With the out-of-fold predictions, `r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "others")` clips of other bellbirds were classified as one of these species, which allows estimating the focal vs others contrast.

```{r symp allo contrast model}
priors1b <- c(prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = "Intercept"), prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b"),
              prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"))

mod1b <- brm(mimic_type ~ vocalizing_type + (1 | recording), data = d1,
             family = bernoulli(), prior = priors1b, chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = cores,
             control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), seed = 123,
             file = file.path(fit_dir, "sympatric_allopatric_focal_vs_others"), file_refit = "on_change")
```

```{r mod1b summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| fig-height: 3

extended_summary(mod1b, n.posterior = 1000, fill = mako(10)[8], trace.palette = mako,
                 remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE)
```

```{r mod1b ppc}
#| fig-height: 3

custom_ppc(mod1b, group = "vocalizing_type")
```

```{r mod1 estimates}
p_focal1 <- plogis(as_draws_df(mod1)$b_Intercept)
ratio_focal1 <- p_focal1 / (1 - p_focal1)

post1b <- as_draws_df(mod1b)
p_others1b <- plogis(post1b$b_Intercept)
p_focal1b <- plogis(post1b$b_Intercept + post1b$b_vocalizing_typefocal)
or1b <- exp(post1b$b_vocalizing_typefocal)
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

#### Summary

- When a focal bellbird vocalization was classified as a heterospecific, it was the sympatric species with probability `r ci(p_focal1)`, i.e. `r ci(ratio_focal1, 1)` times more often than its allopatric relative (`r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "focal" & d1$mimic_type == 1)` vs `r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "focal" & d1$mimic_type == 0)` clips)

- Other bellbirds were rarely classified as any of these species (`r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "others")` of `r sum(bb_sa$vocalizing_type == "others")` clips; `r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "others" & d1$mimic_type == 1)` sympatric). Probability that such a classification is the sympatric species: other bellbirds `r ci(p_others1b)`, focal bellbird `r ci(p_focal1b)`; odds ratio focal vs others `r ci(or1b, 1)`

:::

# Only sympatric species

Is the focal bellbird classified as a heterospecific (instead of its own species) more often than other bellbirds? Unassigned clips are excluded.

```{r symp data}
bb_s <- build("sympatric")
bb_s$vocalizing_type <- factor(bb_s$vocalizing_type, levels = c("others", "focal"))
kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(`Classified as` = bb_s$predicted_sp, bb_s$vocalizing_type)))

d2 <- bb_s[bb_s$predicted_sp != "Unassigned", ]
d2$prediction_type <- as.integer(d2$predicted_sp != "Procnias tricarunculatus")
```

```{r symp model}
priors2 <- c(prior(normal(-3, 1), class = "Intercept"), prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b"),
             prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"))

mod2 <- brm(prediction_type ~ vocalizing_type + (1 | recording), data = d2,
            family = bernoulli(), prior = priors2, chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = cores,
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 15), seed = 123,
            file = file.path(fit_dir, "sympatric_only"), file_refit = "on_change")
```

```{r mod2 summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| fig-height: 3

extended_summary(mod2, n.posterior = 1000, fill = mako(10)[8], trace.palette = mako,
                 remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE)
```

```{r mod2 ppc}
#| fig-height: 3

custom_ppc(mod2, group = "vocalizing_type")
```

```{r mod2 estimates}
post2 <- as_draws_df(mod2)
or2 <- exp(post2$b_vocalizing_typefocal)
p_focal2 <- as.numeric(posterior_epred(mod2, newdata = data.frame(vocalizing_type = "focal", recording = NA), re_formula = NA))
p_others2 <- as.numeric(posterior_epred(mod2, newdata = data.frame(vocalizing_type = "others", recording = NA), re_formula = NA))
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

#### Summary

- `r sum(d2$vocalizing_type == "focal" & d2$prediction_type == 1)` of `r sum(d2$vocalizing_type == "focal")` assigned focal bellbird vocalizations were classified as a sympatric model species (predicted probability `r ci(p_focal2)`), against `r sum(d2$vocalizing_type == "others" & d2$prediction_type == 1)` of `r sum(d2$vocalizing_type == "others")` vocalizations of other bellbirds (`r ci(p_others2, 3)`)
- Odds ratio focal vs other bellbirds: `r ci(or2, 0)`

:::

# Mimicry through time

Daily proportions of the focal bellbird vocalizations assigned to each category by the cross-validated sympatric-only classifier. Montezuma Oropendola (`r sum(focal_pred$sympatric$predicted == "Psarocolius montezuma")` clips) is not modeled. Clips below their species' threshold are unassigned.

```{r time data}
rec_info <- read.table("./data/raw/Recording_dates_.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ";", encoding = "latin1")
# file names are matched on their ASCII characters only: the table is Latin-1 and the "ó" of the
# phone recordings "Nueva-grabación-*.wav" is corrupted in it, so exact matching dropped them
file_key <- function(x) gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "", iconv(x, "UTF-8", "ASCII", sub = ""), useBytes = TRUE)
rec_info$key <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "", rec_info$sound.files, useBytes = TRUE)
# dates are written with Spanish month abbreviations (e.g. 05-ago-20); they are converted to
# month numbers so that parsing does not depend on the locale
rec_info$date <- gsub("/", "-", rec_info$date)
month_num <- c(ene = 1, feb = 2, mar = 3, abr = 4, may = 5, jun = 6, jul = 7, ago = 8, sep = 9, set = 9,
               oct = 10, nov = 11, dic = 12)
dp <- strsplit(rec_info$date, "-")
rec_info$date <- as.Date(sprintf("20%s-%02d-%s", sapply(dp, `[`, 3), month_num[sapply(dp, `[`, 2)], sapply(dp, `[`, 1)))

fp <- focal_pred$sympatric
fp$recording <- focal_meta$recording[match(fp$clip, focal_meta$clip)]
fp$date <- rec_info$date[match(file_key(fp$recording), rec_info$key)]
cat(sum(is.na(fp$date)), "clips without a recording date\n")
fp <- fp[!is.na(fp$date), ]

cats <- c("Procnias tricarunculatus", "Pteroglossus torquatus", "Ramphastos sulfuratus", "Unassigned")
dat <- as.data.frame(table(date = fp$date, pred = factor(fp$predicted, levels = c(cats, "Psarocolius montezuma"))))
names(dat)[3] <- "n"
dat$date <- as.Date(as.character(dat$date))
dat$total <- ave(dat$n, dat$date, FUN = sum)
dat <- dat[dat$pred %in% cats, ]
dat$prop <- dat$n / dat$total
dat$pred_common_name <- factor(common_names[as.character(dat$pred)], levels = common_names[cats])
dat$julian_day <- as.numeric(format(dat$date, "%j"))
dat$obs <- factor(seq_len(nrow(dat)))
dat$day <- factor(dat$date)

kable(aggregate(n ~ pred_common_name, dat, sum), col.names = c("Category", "Clips"))
```

Binomial model (logit link): Julian day with intercepts and slopes varying by category, a random intercept of recording day (the categories of a day share it, and date varies only between days) and an observation-level random effect for overdispersion.

```{r time model}
priors3 <- c(prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = "Intercept"), prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"),
             prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"))

mod3 <- brm(n | trials(total) ~ scale(julian_day) + (1 + scale(julian_day) | pred_common_name) + (1 | day) + (1 | obs),
            family = binomial, data = dat, prior = priors3, chains = chains, cores = cores, iter = iter,
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), seed = 123,
            file = file.path(fit_dir, "mimicry_through_time"), file_refit = "on_change")
```

```{r mod3 summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| fig-height: 3

extended_summary(mod3, n.posterior = 1000, fill = mako(10)[8], trace.palette = mako,
                 remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE)
```

```{r mod3 ppc}
#| fig-height: 3

custom_ppc(mod3)
```

Slope of each category (log-odds per SD of Julian day):

```{r slopes}
slopes <- function(fit) {
    post <- as.data.frame(fit)
    cols <- grep("^r_pred_common_name\\[.*,scalejulian_day\\]$", names(post), value = TRUE)
    s <- sapply(cols, function(cl) post$b_scalejulian_day + post[[cl]])
    colnames(s) <- gsub("\\.", " ", sub("r_pred_common_name\\[(.*),scalejulian_day\\]", "\\1", cols))
    data.frame(Category = colnames(s), Slope = colMeans(s),
               `2.5%` = apply(s, 2, quantile, 0.025), `97.5%` = apply(s, 2, quantile, 0.975),
               check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}
sl3 <- slopes(mod3)
kable(sl3, digits = 3)
```

```{r time plot}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

nd <- expand.grid(julian_day = seq(min(dat$julian_day), max(dat$julian_day), length.out = 100),
                  pred_common_name = levels(dat$pred_common_name), total = 100)
nd$fit_prop <- colMeans(posterior_epred(mod3, newdata = nd,
                                        re_formula = ~ (1 + scale(julian_day) | pred_common_name))) / 100
nd$date <- as.Date(nd$julian_day - 1, origin = paste0(format(dat$date[1], "%Y"), "-01-01"))

ggplot(dat[dat$prop > 0, ], aes(date, prop, fill = pred_common_name, color = pred_common_name)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = n), pch = 21) +
    geom_line(data = nd, aes(y = fit_prop), linewidth = 1.2) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(alpha = 0.6, end = 0.8) +
    scale_color_viridis_d(alpha = 0.8, end = 0.8) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = "Date", y = "Percentage of vocalizations\npredicted as", fill = "Predicted species",
         color = "Predicted species", size = "Number of recorded\nvocalizations") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.5))
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

#### Summary

- The proportion of focal bellbird vocalizations classified as its own species increased over time (slope `r round(sl3$Slope[sl3$Category == "Three-wattled Bellbird"], 2)` [95% UI: `r round(sl3[["2.5%"]][sl3$Category == "Three-wattled Bellbird"], 2)`–`r round(sl3[["97.5%"]][sl3$Category == "Three-wattled Bellbird"], 2)`])
- The proportions classified as Keel-billed Toucan and Collared Aracari tended to decrease, but their intervals include zero; unassigned vocalizations showed no trend

:::

# Quality of imitations and consistency of own song through time

Did the imitations get closer to their models over time, did the focal bellbird's own song get closer to that of other bellbirds, and did both become more consistent? Each focal bellbird clip assigned to Keel-billed Toucan, Collared Aracari or Three-wattled Bellbird by the sympatric-only classifier is described by two measures, both computed from the generic BirdNET embeddings (not the custom classifiers):

- **Acoustic similarity**: neighbour similarity, the mean cosine similarity to the 5 most similar reference clips of the assigned species. Similarity to the nearest real vocalizations, rather than to a species centroid, does not penalize a good copy of one variant of an acoustically variable species
- **Consistency**: the mean cosine similarity to each of the other clips of the same type recorded on the same day

Only clips assigned to a species are used, so the measures describe how good the imitations (or own songs) were, not how many there were (see [Mimicry through time](#mimicry-through-time)). Recording conditions changed through the season, so both measures were modelled with long-window signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and recording equipment as covariates.

```{r quality data}
read_emb <- function(f) {
    e <- read.csv(f, encoding = "latin1")
    clip <- sub("\\.wav$", "", sub(".*\\\\", "", iconv(e$file_path, "latin1", "UTF-8")))
    m <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(e$embedding, ","), as.numeric))
    m <- m / sqrt(rowSums(m^2)) # unit length, so that dot products are cosine similarities
    rownames(m) <- clip
    m
}
emb_focal <- read_emb("./data/processed/embeddings/embeddings_mimic.csv")
emb_ref <- read_emb("./data/processed/embeddings/embeddings_sympatric_allopatric_spp.csv")
ref_sp <- folds$species[match(paste0(rownames(emb_ref), ".wav"), folds$clip)]
ref_rec_all <- folds$recording[match(paste0(rownames(emb_ref), ".wav"), folds$clip)]

quality_spp <- c("Ramphastos sulfuratus", "Pteroglossus torquatus", "Procnias tricarunculatus")
q <- fp[fp$predicted %in% quality_spp, ]
q$species <- factor(common_names[q$predicted], levels = common_names[quality_spp])
q$julian_day <- as.numeric(format(q$date, "%j"))
q$day <- factor(q$date)
q$equipment <- rec_info$equipment[match(file_key(q$recording), rec_info$key)]
```

## Recording quality

Vocalizations recorded with low SNR have embeddings partly describing the background noise, so they look less similar to any species. The equipment changed through the season (Tascam DR-40 in April, mostly iPhone SE in July–August, Tascam DR-40 with Sennheiser microphone in September–November), so recording quality could create or hide a temporal trend. The random intercepts of day do not remove this, because date varies only between days.

SNR was measured from the original recordings within the annotated frequency band of each clip, against up to 0.5 s of noise before and after it, leaving out any other annotated vocalization (long-window SNR). Noise was also measured in fixed bands (the median annotated band of the focal clips assigned to each species): the difference in noise level between two bands does not depend on recording gain, so it shows whether recording conditions changed differently for each vocalization type.

```{r snr long}
snr_long_file <- "./data/processed/snr_long_focal.csv"
if (!file.exists(snr_long_file)) {
    est_attr <- attr(readRDS("./data/processed/extended_selection_table_sympatric_and_allopatric_species.RDS"), "check.res")
    ann <- read.csv("./data/processed/pooled_annotations.csv")
    ann <- ann[ann$source == "mimetic_bellbird", ]
    fq <- data.frame(clip = est_attr$sound.files, file = est_attr$orig.sound.files, start = est_attr$orig.start, end = est_attr$orig.end)
    fq <- fq[fq$clip %in% q$clip, ]
    fq <- merge(fq, q[, c("clip", "predicted")], by = "clip")
    fq$bottom <- ann$bottom.freq[match(paste(fq$file, fq$start), paste(ann$sound.files, ann$start))]
    fq$top <- ann$top.freq[match(paste(fq$file, fq$start), paste(ann$sound.files, ann$start))]
    # fixed bands: median annotated band of the focal clips assigned to each species
    bands <- lapply(split(fq, fq$predicted), function(d) c(median(d$bottom, na.rm = TRUE), median(d$top, na.rm = TRUE)))
    win <- 0.5
    band_power <- function(sp, rng) {
        w <- sp$freq >= rng[1] & sp$freq <= rng[2]
        colMeans(10^(sp$amp[w, , drop = FALSE] / 10))
    }
    res <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(fq)), function(i) {
        x <- fq[i, ]
        dur <- tuneR::readWave(file.path("./data/raw/recordings", x$file), header = TRUE)
        dur <- dur$samples / dur$sample.rate
        from <- max(0, x$start - win); to <- min(dur, x$end + win)
        wv <- tuneR::readWave(file.path("./data/raw/recordings", x$file), from = from, to = to, units = "seconds")
        if (wv@stereo) wv <- tuneR::mono(wv, "left")
        sp <- seewave::spectro(wv, wl = 512, ovlp = 50, plot = FALSE, dB = "max0")
        tt <- sp$time + from
        # noise frames: within the windows, outside every annotated vocalization of the recording
        a <- ann[ann$sound.files == x$file, ]
        in_voc <- sapply(tt, function(t) any(t >= a$start & t <= a$end))
        sig <- tt >= x$start & tt <= x$end
        noise <- !in_voc & !sig
        own <- c(x$bottom, x$top)
        p_own <- band_power(sp, own)
        out <- data.frame(clip = x$clip, noise_frames = sum(noise),
                          snr_long = if (sum(noise) >= 3) 10 * log10(mean(p_own[sig]) / mean(p_own[noise])) else NA)
        for (b in names(bands)) out[[paste0("noise_", b)]] <- if (sum(noise) >= 3) 10 * log10(mean(band_power(sp, bands[[b]])[noise])) else NA
        out
    }, mc.cores = cores)
    snr_long <- do.call(rbind, res)
    write.csv(snr_long, snr_long_file, row.names = FALSE)
}
snr_long <- read.csv(snr_long_file)
q$snr_long <- snr_long$snr_long[match(q$clip, snr_long$clip)]
noise_cols <- grep("^noise_P|^noise_R", names(snr_long), value = TRUE)
for (nc in noise_cols) q[[nc]] <- snr_long[[nc]][match(q$clip, snr_long$clip)]
q$noise_bellbird_vs_toucan <- q$noise_Procnias.tricarunculatus - q$noise_Ramphastos.sulfuratus
q$noise_aracari_vs_toucan <- q$noise_Pteroglossus.torquatus - q$noise_Ramphastos.sulfuratus

# clips used in the models: long-window SNR available, and not recorded with the Nikon P900
# (too few clips to estimate its effect)
q_m <- q[!is.na(q$snr_long) & q$equipment != "Nikon P900", ]

kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(q_m$equipment, format(q_m$date, "%b"))[, c("Apr", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov")]),
      caption = "Clips used in the models by equipment and month")
```

Does recording quality change through time differently for each vocalization type?

```{r snr long models}
priors4 <- c(prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"), prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"), prior(exponential(1), class = "sigma"))
priors5 <- priors4
fit_q <- function(formula, data, name) brm(formula, data = data, prior = priors4, chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = cores,
                                           control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), seed = 123,
                                           file = file.path(fit_dir, name), file_refit = "on_change")
q_l <- q[!is.na(q$snr_long), ]
mod8 <- list(
    snr_long = fit_q(scale(snr_long) ~ species * scale(julian_day) + (1 | day/recording), q_l, "snr_long_through_time"),
    noise_bt = fit_q(scale(noise_bellbird_vs_toucan) ~ scale(julian_day) + (1 | day/recording), q_l, "noise_bellbird_vs_toucan_band_through_time"),
    noise_at = fit_q(scale(noise_aracari_vs_toucan) ~ scale(julian_day) + (1 | day/recording), q_l, "noise_aracari_vs_toucan_band_through_time"))

species_slopes <- function(fit, measure) {
    post <- as_draws_df(fit)
    base <- post$b_scalejulian_day
    s <- cbind(base,
               base + post[["b_speciesCollaredAracari:scalejulian_day"]],
               base + post[["b_speciesThreeMwattledBellbird:scalejulian_day"]])
    colnames(s) <- levels(q$species)
    data.frame(Measure = measure, Species = colnames(s), Slope = colMeans(s),
               `2.5%` = apply(s, 2, quantile, 0.025), `97.5%` = apply(s, 2, quantile, 0.975),
               check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}
day_slope <- function(fit, label) {
    x <- as_draws_df(fit)$b_scalejulian_day
    data.frame(Response = label, Slope = mean(x), `2.5%` = quantile(x, 0.025), `97.5%` = quantile(x, 0.975), check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}
sl8 <- species_slopes(mod8$snr_long, "Long-window SNR")
kable(rbind(data.frame(Response = paste("Long-window SNR,", sl8$Species), sl8[, c("Slope", "2.5%", "97.5%")], check.names = FALSE),
            day_slope(mod8$noise_bt, "Noise in bellbird band minus toucan band"),
            day_slope(mod8$noise_at, "Noise in aracari band minus toucan band")),
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Slopes through time (SD per SD of date)")
```

## Acoustic similarity

For each focal clip, neighbour similarity is the mean cosine similarity to its 5 most similar reference clips of the assigned species. Species have different numbers of reference clips, and more clips give closer neighbours by chance, so the reference clips of each species were subsampled to the size of the smallest (`r min(table(ref_sp[ref_sp %in% quality_spp]))` clips), 20 times, and the values averaged. The same score was computed for each reference clip against the subsampled reference clips of its species from other recordings; the **typicality percentile** of a focal clip is its percentile in that distribution (50%: as close to the species as a typical real vocalization).

```{r neighbour similarity}
k_nn <- 5; n_draw <- 20
n_sub <- min(table(ref_sp[ref_sp %in% quality_spp]))
knn_mean <- function(sim) apply(sim, 1, function(x) mean(sort(x, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(k_nn)]))

set.seed(123)
q$knn <- q$pct <- NA
ref_knn <- list()
for (sp in quality_spp) {
    idx <- which(ref_sp == sp)
    qi <- which(q$predicted == sp)
    fk <- pc <- matrix(NA, length(qi), n_draw)
    rk <- matrix(NA, length(idx), n_draw)
    for (d in seq_len(n_draw)) {
        sub <- sample(idx, n_sub)
        fk[, d] <- knn_mean(emb_focal[q$clip[qi], ] %*% t(emb_ref[sub, ]))
        sim_r <- emb_ref[idx, ] %*% t(emb_ref[sub, ])
        sim_r[outer(ref_rec_all[idx], ref_rec_all[sub], "==")] <- -Inf # no neighbours from the same recording
        rk[, d] <- knn_mean(sim_r)
        pc[, d] <- ecdf(rk[, d])(fk[, d])
    }
    q$knn[qi] <- rowMeans(fk); q$pct[qi] <- rowMeans(pc)
    ref_knn[[sp]] <- data.frame(species = unname(common_names[sp]), knn = rowMeans(rk))
}
ref_knn <- do.call(rbind, ref_knn)
ref_knn$species <- factor(ref_knn$species, levels = levels(q$species))
q_m$knn <- q$knn[match(q_m$clip, q$clip)]

kable(data.frame(Species = levels(q_m$species), Clips = as.numeric(table(q_m$species)),
                 Days = tapply(q_m$day, q_m$species, function(x) length(unique(x))),
                 `Focal: neighbour similarity` = tapply(q$knn, q$species, mean),
                 `Reference: neighbour similarity` = tapply(ref_knn$knn, ref_knn$species, mean),
                 `Focal: median typicality percentile` = tapply(q$pct, q$species, median),
                 check.names = FALSE), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

Gaussian model of the standardized neighbour similarity with vocalization type, date (Julian day), their interaction, long-window SNR and equipment, and random intercepts of recording day and of recording within day (date varies only between days, so the day is the unit of replication for the temporal trend):

```{r similarity model}
mod_sim <- fit_q(scale(knn) ~ species * scale(julian_day) + scale(snr_long) + equipment + (1 | day/recording), q_m,
                 "imitation_knn_snrlong_equipment_through_time")
```

```{r similarity summary}
#| fig-height: 5

                 remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE)
```


## Consistency

During vocal learning, copies typically become both more similar to the target and more consistent. Consistency is the variability within a time window (the recording day): for each clip, the mean cosine similarity of its embedding to each of the other clips of the same type recorded on the same day (day × type combinations with at least 5 clips). Higher values mean more consistent. Unlike the similarity to a centroid of the day's clips, the expected value of this mean pairwise similarity does not depend on the number of clips of the day (only its precision does), which matters because the number of own-song clips per day increased through the season. The model has the same structure as that of acoustic similarity. Three checks: the (log) number of clips of the day × type as a covariate; the residual SD modelled as a function of the (log) number of clips (the mean pairwise similarity of a clip in a large group is less noisy, so these clips get more weight, with the amount estimated from the data rather than fixed through weights); and a rarefied version in which each day × type combination is repeatedly subsampled to 5 clips (`r 100` draws) and its mean pairwise similarity averaged across draws, modelled at the level of the combination.

```{r consistency}
qc <- q_m
qc$day_type <- paste(qc$day, qc$species)
grp_n <- table(qc$day_type)
qc <- qc[qc$day_type %in% names(grp_n)[grp_n >= 5], ]
qc$n_group <- as.numeric(grp_n[qc$day_type])
# mean pairwise similarity to the other clips of the group (embeddings are unit length):
# (x . sum of the group - x . x) / (n - 1)
pairwise_mean <- function(emb, group) {
    grp_sum <- rowsum(emb, group)[group, , drop = FALSE]
    (rowSums(emb * grp_sum) - 1) / (as.numeric(table(group)[group]) - 1)
}
qc$consistency <- pairwise_mean(emb_focal[qc$clip, ], qc$day_type)

# rarefied: each group subsampled to 5 clips, mean pairwise similarity averaged over 100 draws
rarefy_pairwise <- function(emb, clips, k = 5, n_draw = 100) {
    mean(replicate(n_draw, { e <- emb[sample(clips, k), ]; sm <- tcrossprod(e); mean(sm[upper.tri(sm)]) }))
}
set.seed(123)
qc_g <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(qc, qc$day_type), function(d)
    data.frame(day = d$day[1], species = d$species[1], julian_day = d$julian_day[1], n_group = nrow(d),
               consistency = rarefy_pairwise(emb_focal, d$clip), snr_long = mean(d$snr_long),
               equipment = names(which.max(table(d$equipment))))))
qc_g$species <- factor(qc_g$species, levels = levels(qc$species))

kable(data.frame(Species = levels(qc$species),
                 Clips = as.numeric(table(qc$species)),
                 `Day × type groups` = tapply(qc$day_type, qc$species, function(x) length(unique(x))),
                 `Mean consistency` = tapply(qc$consistency, qc$species, mean), check.names = FALSE),
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

mod_cons <- fit_q(scale(consistency) ~ species * scale(julian_day) + scale(snr_long) + equipment + (1 | day/recording),
                  qc, "consistency_pairwise_snrlong_equipment_through_time")
mod_cons_n <- fit_q(scale(consistency) ~ species * scale(julian_day) + scale(log(n_group)) + scale(snr_long) + equipment + (1 | day/recording),
                    qc, "consistency_pairwise_snrlong_equipment_n_through_time")
mod_cons_r <- fit_q(scale(consistency) ~ species * scale(julian_day) + scale(snr_long) + equipment + (1 | day),
                    qc_g, "consistency_rarefied_snrlong_equipment_through_time")
# residual SD as a function of the number of clips of the group (log scale)
priors_sigma <- c(prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"), prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"),
                  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b", dpar = "sigma"))
fit_sigma <- function(formula, data, name) brm(bf(formula, sigma ~ scale(log(n_group))), data = data, prior = priors_sigma,
                                               chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = cores, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
                                               seed = 123, file = file.path(fit_dir, name), file_refit = "on_change")
mod_cons_s <- fit_sigma(scale(consistency) ~ species * scale(julian_day) + scale(snr_long) + equipment + (1 | day/recording),
                        qc, "consistency_pairwise_snrlong_equipment_sigma_through_time")
sigma_n <- function(fit, model) {
    x <- as_draws_df(fit)$b_sigma_scalelogn_group
    data.frame(Model = model, Estimate = mean(x), `2.5%` = quantile(x, 0.025), `97.5%` = quantile(x, 0.975),
               check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}
```

## Trends

```{r quality slopes}
# difference from the slope of the toucan-like vocalizations of the same recordings, reported only
# when at least one of the two slopes compared has a 95% UI excluding zero
slope_diff <- function(fit, measure) {
    post <- as_draws_df(fit)
    sl <- slq[slq$Measure == measure, ]
    clear <- setNames(sl[["2.5%"]] > 0 | sl[["97.5%"]] < 0, sl$Species)
    cmp <- c(`Bellbird minus toucan` = "Three-wattled Bellbird", `Aracari minus toucan` = "Collared Aracari")
    cmp <- cmp[clear[cmp] | clear[["Keel-billed Toucan"]]]
    if (!length(cmp)) return(NULL)
    d <- sapply(cmp, function(sp) post[[paste0("b_species", gsub(" ", "", gsub("-", "M", sp)), ":scalejulian_day")]])
    d <- matrix(d, ncol = length(cmp))
    data.frame(Measure = measure, Comparison = names(cmp),
               Difference = colMeans(d), `2.5%` = apply(d, 2, quantile, 0.025), `97.5%` = apply(d, 2, quantile, 0.975),
               check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}
slq <- rbind(species_slopes(mod_sim, "Acoustic similarity"), species_slopes(mod_cons, "Consistency"))
kable(slq, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Slopes through time of each vocalization type (SD per SD of date)")
sdq <- rbind(slope_diff(mod_sim, "Acoustic similarity"), slope_diff(mod_cons, "Consistency"))
kable(sdq, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Difference from the slope of the toucan-like vocalizations of the same recordings (the comparison least affected by recording artifacts), only where at least one of the two slopes has a 95% UI excluding zero")
cov_eff <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list(`Acoustic similarity` = mod_sim, Consistency = mod_cons), function(f) {
    s <- as.data.frame(fixef(f))
    s <- s[grepl("snr_long|equipment", rownames(s)), ]
    data.frame(Term = rownames(s), s[, c("Estimate", "Q2.5", "Q97.5")], row.names = NULL)
}))
cov_eff <- cbind(Measure = rep(c("Acoustic similarity", "Consistency"), each = nrow(cov_eff) / 2), cov_eff)
kable(cov_eff, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Effects of long-window SNR (per SD) and equipment (relative to the iPhone SE), SD of the measure")
cons_chk <- rbind(cbind(Version = "Main model", species_slopes(mod_cons, "Consistency")),
                  cbind(Version = "+ log number of clips of the day", species_slopes(mod_cons_n, "Consistency")),
                  cbind(Version = "Residual SD depends on log number of clips of the day", species_slopes(mod_cons_s, "Consistency")),
                  cbind(Version = "Rarefied to 5 clips per day (one value per day × type)", species_slopes(mod_cons_r, "Consistency")))
kable(cons_chk[, c("Version", "Species", "Slope", "2.5%", "97.5%")], digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Consistency slopes in the main model and the three sample-size checks")
kable(sigma_n(mod_cons_s, "Consistency by type"), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Effect of the log number of clips of the day × type on the log residual SD (negative: larger groups less noisy)")
```

```{r quality plot}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

# population-level fits at average long-window SNR, averaged over equipment (weighted by number of clips)
quality_curves <- function(fit, d, y, measure) {
    grid <- expand.grid(julian_day = seq(min(d$julian_day), max(d$julian_day), length.out = 50),
                        species = levels(d$species), equipment = sort(unique(d$equipment)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    grid$snr_long <- mean(d$snr_long)
    w <- as.numeric(table(d$equipment)[grid$equipment]) / nrow(d)
    ep <- posterior_epred(fit, newdata = grid, re_formula = NA) * sd(d[[y]]) + mean(d[[y]])
    key <- paste(grid$julian_day, grid$species)
    ep <- t(rowsum(t(ep) * w, key, reorder = FALSE))
    g <- grid[!duplicated(key), c("julian_day", "species")]
    data.frame(g, date = as.Date(g$julian_day - 1, origin = "2020-01-01"), measure = measure, value = colMeans(ep),
               low = apply(ep, 2, quantile, 0.025), high = apply(ep, 2, quantile, 0.975))
}
fits <- rbind(quality_curves(mod_sim, q_m, "knn", "Acoustic similarity"), quality_curves(mod_cons, qc, "consistency", "Consistency"))
fits$species <- factor(fits$species, levels = levels(q$species))
ql <- rbind(data.frame(q_m[, c("date", "species")], measure = "Acoustic similarity", value = q_m$knn),
            data.frame(qc[, c("date", "species")], measure = "Consistency", value = qc$consistency))

ggplot(ql, aes(date, value, color = species, fill = species)) +
    geom_jitter(width = 1, height = 0, alpha = 0.25, size = 1) +
    geom_ribbon(data = fits, aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
    geom_line(data = fits, linewidth = 1.2) +
    facet_grid(measure ~ species, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.8, guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.8, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 months", date_labels = "%b") +
    labs(x = "Date", y = NULL) +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank())
```

Lines and bands: posterior mean and 95% interval of the population-level fit at average long-window SNR, averaged over equipment in proportion to its number of clips.

#### Summary

```{r quality summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| echo: false

# a bound that is not zero but rounds to 0.00 is shown with 3 decimals, so it is not read as touching zero
f2 <- function(x) ifelse(round(x, 2) == 0 & x != 0, sprintf("%.3f", x), sprintf("%.2f", x))
ui <- function(est, lo, hi) sprintf("%s [95%% UI: %s–%s]", f2(est), f2(lo), f2(hi))
fq_ <- function(meas, sp) {
    r <- slq[slq$Measure == meas & slq$Species == sp, ]
    ui(r$Slope, r[["2.5%"]], r[["97.5%"]])
}
fd_ <- function(meas, cmp) {
    r <- sdq[sdq$Measure == meas & sdq$Comparison == cmp, ]
    ui(r$Difference, r[["2.5%"]], r[["97.5%"]])
}
fds <- function(fit) with(day_slope(fit, ""), ui(Slope, `2.5%`, `97.5%`))
for (m in c("Acoustic similarity", "Consistency"))
    cat("- ", m, " through time (slope, SD per SD of date; long-window SNR and equipment as covariates): Keel-billed Toucan ", fq_(m, "Keel-billed Toucan"),
        ", Collared Aracari ", fq_(m, "Collared Aracari"), ", Three-wattled Bellbird ", fq_(m, "Three-wattled Bellbird"),
        if (any(sdq$Measure == m)) paste0("; ", paste(sapply(sdq$Comparison[sdq$Measure == m], function(cmp) paste(tolower(cmp), fd_(m, cmp))), collapse = ", ")),
        "\n", sep = "")
cat("- Noise in the bellbird band relative to the toucan band through time: ", fds(mod8$noise_bt),
    "; aracari band relative to the toucan band: ", fds(mod8$noise_at), "\n", sep = "")
cat("- Consistency slopes of the own song in the sample-size checks: ",
    paste(sprintf("%s %s [%s–%s]", tolower(cons_chk$Version[cons_chk$Species == "Three-wattled Bellbird"]),
                  f2(cons_chk$Slope[cons_chk$Species == "Three-wattled Bellbird"]), f2(cons_chk[["2.5%"]][cons_chk$Species == "Three-wattled Bellbird"]),
                  f2(cons_chk[["97.5%"]][cons_chk$Species == "Three-wattled Bellbird"])), collapse = "; "), "\n", sep = "")
```

:::

# Dialects of the focal bellbird

Three-wattled Bellbirds sing in regional dialects. If the focal bellbird produced more than one dialect, and in proportions that changed through time, a day centroid that mixes dialects would make its own song look less consistent, and a shift towards the dialect closer to the reference recordings could look like an improvement. A BirdNET classifier was trained to discriminate the dialects of the reference bellbirds (annotated as Monteverde, Nicaragua, Panama and Talamanca; babbling left out), with the same pipeline as the species classifiers: 5-fold cross-validation grouped by recording and stratified by dialect (seed 123), bandpass 400–12,000 Hz, per-dialect thresholds maximizing F1 on the out-of-fold predictions, and the configuration chosen with the one-standard-error rule among the same 30 random configurations compared for the species classifiers (`MODELS=dialect bash scripts/birdnet_cv.sh`). The focal bellbird clips classified as Three-wattled Bellbird by the sympatric-only classifier were then classified by the ensemble of the 5 fold models.

## Dialect classifier

```{r dialect classifier}
species_cv_dir <- cv_dir
dialect_dir <- "./data/processed/birdnet_cv_dialect"
dialects <- c("Monteverde", "Nicaragua", "Panama", "Talamanca")
dfolds <- read.csv(file.path(dialect_dir, "folds.csv"))
# same 30 random configurations as the species classifiers
dialect_configs <- read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "random_search_configs.csv"))$config

# the CV functions read cv_dir and model_spp
cv_dir <- dialect_dir
model_spp$dialect <- dialects
dscores <- setNames(lapply(dialect_configs, oof_scores, model = "dialect", folds = dfolds), dialect_configs)
# configurations whose training diverged (over 90% of the clips never reach the 0.05 reporting
# limit in some fold) are left out
d_diverged <- dialect_configs[sapply(dscores, function(sc) any(tapply(rowSums(sc[, dialects]) == 0, sc$fold, mean) > 0.9))]
dialect_configs <- setdiff(dialect_configs, d_diverged)
dscores <- dscores[dialect_configs]
d_auprc <- sapply(dscores, function(sc) mean(sapply(dialects, function(d) avg_precision(sc[[d]], sc$true == d))))
d_fold <- sapply(dscores, fold_auprc, spp = dialects)
d_cx <- do.call(rbind, lapply(dialect_configs, config_complexity, model = "dialect"))
d_best <- select_one_se(d_auprc, sd(d_fold[, which.max(d_auprc)]) / sqrt(5), d_cx)
d_thr <- optimal_thresholds(dscores[[d_best]], dialects)
d_metrics <- cv_metrics(dscores[[d_best]], dialects, d_thr)
d_focal <- ensemble_scores(d_best, "dialect")
# performance of the selection procedure itself (configuration and thresholds chosen without the scored fold)
d_sel <- selection_excluded_metrics(dscores, dialects, d_cx)
cv_dir <- species_cv_dir

d_tab <- data.frame(Configuration = dialect_configs, `Macro AUPRC` = d_auprc, `AUPRC SD across folds` = apply(d_fold, 2, sd),
                    Selected = ifelse(dialect_configs == d_best, "yes", ""), check.names = FALSE)
kable(d_tab[order(-d_tab$`Macro AUPRC`), ], digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = paste0("Out-of-fold macro AUPRC of each configuration (diverged and left out: ",
                       if (length(d_diverged)) paste(d_diverged, collapse = ", ") else "none", ")"))
kable(data.frame(`Selected configuration: mean fold macro AUPRC` = mean(d_fold[, d_best]),
                 `Selection procedure: macro AUPRC` = mean(d_sel$AUPRC), `Selection procedure: macro F1` = mean(d_sel$F1),
                 `Configurations chosen across folds` = paste(sort(unique(d_sel$chosen)), collapse = ", "), check.names = FALSE),
      digits = 3, caption = "Optimism of the selection: each fold scored with the configuration and thresholds chosen on the other four")
kable(setNames(d_metrics$per_species, c("Dialect", "Precision", "Recall", "F1", "AUPRC", "Threshold", "Clips")),
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, caption = paste0("Out-of-fold performance of the selected configuration (", d_best, ")"))

dsc <- dscores[[d_best]]
dsc$pred <- d_metrics$pred
dsc$recording <- dfolds$recording[match(paste0(dsc$clip, ".wav"), dfolds$clip)]
# recording-level dialect: highest mean confidence across the recording's clips
rec_d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(dsc, dsc$recording), function(d)
    data.frame(true = d$true[1], pred = dialects[which.max(colMeans(d[, dialects]))])))
```

Out-of-fold confusion matrix (assigned clips, rows: annotated dialect) and recording-level accuracy (dialect with the highest mean confidence over the clips of each recording):

```{r dialect confusion}
d_tab <- table(Annotated = dsc$true, Predicted = factor(dsc$pred, levels = c(dialects, "Unassigned")))
r_tab <- table(Annotated = rec_d$true, Predicted = factor(rec_d$pred, levels = dialects))
kable(as.data.frame.matrix(d_tab), caption = "Clips (number)")
kable(as.data.frame.matrix(prop.table(d_tab, 1)), digits = 2, caption = "Clips, normalized (proportion of the clips of each annotated dialect)")
kable(as.data.frame.matrix(r_tab),
      caption = paste0("Recordings (number): ", sum(rec_d$true == rec_d$pred), " of ", nrow(rec_d), " correctly assigned"))
kable(as.data.frame.matrix(prop.table(r_tab, 1)), digits = 2, caption = "Recordings, normalized (proportion of the recordings of each annotated dialect)")
```

## Dialects of the focal bellbird

```{r focal dialects}
fd <- q[q$species == "Three-wattled Bellbird", ]
fd <- cbind(fd, d_focal[match(fd$clip, d_focal$clip), dialects])
fd$dialect <- assign_species(fd, dialects, d_thr)
fd$dialect_conf <- apply(fd[, dialects], 1, max)
fd$period <- cut(fd$date, as.Date(c("2020-03-01", "2020-06-01", "2020-08-31", "2020-12-01")),
                 labels = c("April", "July–August", "September–November"))

kable(cbind(as.data.frame.matrix(round(100 * prop.table(dtab, 1), 1)), Clips = rowSums(dtab)),
```

`r sum(nt[, "Nicaragua"] > 0 & nt[, "Talamanca"] > 0)` of the `r sum(nt[, "Nicaragua"] + nt[, "Talamanca"] > 0)` recordings with Nicaragua or Talamanca clips have both, so the focal bellbird alternated between the two dialects within recording sessions.

Change in the proportion of Talamanca rather than Nicaragua clips through time (Bernoulli model, logit link, random intercepts of day and recording within day):

```{r dialect time model}

fnt$talamanca <- as.integer(fnt$dialect == "Talamanca")
mod10 <- brm(talamanca ~ scale(julian_day) + (1 | day/recording), data = fnt, family = bernoulli(),
             prior = c(prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = "Intercept"), prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"), prior(exponential(1), class = "sd")),
             chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = cores, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), seed = 123,
             file = file.path(fit_dir, "focal_dialect_through_time"), file_refit = "on_change")
```

## Own song within dialect

For the focal clips assigned to Nicaragua or Talamanca:

- **Consistency within dialect**: mean cosine similarity of each clip to each of the other clips of the same dialect recorded on the same day (as for the consistency of each vocalization type; day × dialect combinations with at least 5 clips). Higher values mean more consistent. Checks: residual SD modelled as a function of the (log) number of clips of the day × dialect, and rarefied to 5 clips per day × dialect. Benchmark: the same measure for reference clips of the same dialect, relative to the other clips of their own recording (recordings with at least 5 clips)
- **Similarity within dialect**: neighbour similarity (mean cosine similarity to the 5 most similar clips) to the reference clips of the assigned dialect, subsampled 20 times to the size of the smallest of the two (`r min(table(dfolds$species)[c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca")])` clips), and its typicality percentile among the reference clips of that dialect (scored against clips of the same dialect from other recordings)

```{r within dialect measures}
dref <- dfolds
dref$clip <- sub("\\.wav$", "", dref$clip)
dref <- dref[dref$clip %in% rownames(emb_ref), ]

# consistency within day x dialect
fnt$day_dialect <- paste(fnt$day, fnt$dialect)
keep <- names(which(table(fnt$day_dialect) >= 5))
bd <- fnt[fnt$day_dialect %in% keep, ]
bd$n_group <- as.numeric(table(bd$day_dialect)[bd$day_dialect])
bd$consistency <- pairwise_mean(emb_focal[bd$clip, ], bd$day_dialect)
ref_dd <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(dref, paste(dref$recording, dref$species)), function(d) {
    if (nrow(d) < 5) return(NULL)
    data.frame(dialect = d$species[1], consistency = pairwise_mean(emb_ref[d$clip, , drop = FALSE], rep("r", nrow(d))))
}))

# neighbour similarity to the reference clips of the assigned dialect
set.seed(123)
n_sub_d <- min(table(dref$species)[c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca")])
fnt$knn_d <- fnt$pct_d <- NA
for (dl in c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca")) {
    idx <- which(dref$species == dl)
    fi <- which(fnt$dialect == dl)
    fk <- pc <- matrix(NA, length(fi), n_draw)
    for (dr in seq_len(n_draw)) {
        sub <- sample(idx, n_sub_d)
        fk[, dr] <- knn_mean(emb_focal[fnt$clip[fi], ] %*% t(emb_ref[dref$clip[sub], ]))
        sim_r <- emb_ref[dref$clip[idx], ] %*% t(emb_ref[dref$clip[sub], ])
        sim_r[outer(dref$recording[idx], dref$recording[sub], "==")] <- -Inf
        pc[, dr] <- ecdf(knn_mean(sim_r))(fk[, dr])
    }
    fnt$knn_d[fi] <- rowMeans(fk); fnt$pct_d[fi] <- rowMeans(pc)
}

kable(data.frame(Dialect = c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca"),
                 `Focal clips` = as.numeric(table(fnt$dialect)[c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca")]),
                 `Day × dialect groups (≥ 5 clips)` = sapply(c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca"), function(dl) length(unique(bd$day_dialect[bd$dialect == dl]))),
                 `Focal: consistency within day × dialect` = tapply(bd$consistency, bd$dialect, mean)[c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca")],
                 `Other bellbirds: consistency within recording` = tapply(ref_dd$consistency, ref_dd$dialect, mean)[c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca")],
                 `Focal: neighbour similarity to the dialect` = tapply(fnt$knn_d, fnt$dialect, mean)[c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca")],
                 `Focal: median typicality percentile` = tapply(fnt$pct_d, fnt$dialect, median)[c("Nicaragua", "Talamanca")],
                 check.names = FALSE), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

Models of the two measures through time, with dialect, its interaction with date, long-window SNR and recording equipment (as for the vocalization types; clips recorded with the Nikon P900 or without long-window SNR left out):

```{r within dialect models}
    sim_sp = brm(scale(knn) ~ dialect + scale(julian_day) + scale(snr_long) + equipment + (1 | day/recording), data = fnt_l,

    data.frame(day = d$day[1], dialect = d$dialect[1], julian_day = d$julian_day[1], n_group = nrow(d),

# residual SD as a function of the number of clips of the day x dialect (log scale)
mod11_s <- fit_sigma(scale(consistency) ~ dialect * scale(julian_day) + scale(snr_long) + equipment + (1 | day/recording),
```

```{r within dialect slopes}
}
```

# Precision of the trends

Several trends in the vocal-quality and dialect analyses have intervals that include zero. With only 7–10 recording days per vocalization type in some analyses, such intervals may reflect a lack of precision rather than an absence of change. This section quantifies how large a change the data can rule out.

## How large a change the data can rule out

All measures and dates are standardized, so slopes are in SD of the measure per SD of date. A region of practical equivalence (ROPE) of ± `r 0.1` SD per SD of date was used, the conventional "negligible" standardized effect (Kruschke 2018). Given the length of the sampling season, this ROPE is equivalent to a change of about ± `r 0.1` × (season range in SD of date) over the whole season (see the table). Each slope is classified as:

- **Change**: the 95% interval excludes zero
- **Practically no change**: the 95% interval lies entirely within the ROPE
- **Inconclusive**: neither (the data cannot tell a negligible change from a relevant one)

The approximate minimum detectable slope is the slope that would be detected (95% interval excluding zero) with 80% probability given the posterior uncertainty: (1.96 + 0.84) × posterior SD of the slope.

```{r precision of slopes}
rope <- 0.1
type_draws <- function(fit) {
    post <- as_draws_df(fit)
    base <- post$b_scalejulian_day
    cbind(`Keel-billed Toucan` = base, `Collared Aracari` = base + post[["b_speciesCollaredAracari:scalejulian_day"]],
          `Three-wattled Bellbird` = base + post[["b_speciesThreeMwattledBellbird:scalejulian_day"]])
}
dialect_draws <- function(fit) {
    post <- as_draws_df(fit)
    cbind(Nicaragua = post$b_scalejulian_day, Talamanca = post$b_scalejulian_day + post[["b_dialectTalamanca:scalejulian_day"]])
}
precision_rows <- function(draws, measure, data) {
    season <- diff(range(data$julian_day)) / sd(data$julian_day)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(colnames(draws), function(g) {
        x <- draws[, g]; lo <- quantile(x, 0.025); hi <- quantile(x, 0.975)
        data.frame(Measure = measure, Group = g, Slope = mean(x), `2.5%` = lo, `97.5%` = hi,
                   `Change over the season (SD)` = mean(x) * season,
                   `Season change, 95% interval` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", lo * season, hi * season),
                   `P(inside ROPE)` = mean(abs(x) < rope),
                   `Minimum detectable slope` = 2.8 * sd(x),
                   Conclusion = if (lo > 0 | hi < 0) "Change" else if (lo > -rope & hi < rope) "Practically no change" else "Inconclusive",
                   check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
    }))
}
prec <- rbind(precision_rows(type_draws(mod_sim), "Similarity to the assigned species", q_m),
              precision_rows(type_draws(mod_cons), "Consistency (mean pairwise similarity within day × type)", qc),
              precision_rows(dialect_draws(mod11$sim), "Similarity to the assigned dialect", fnt_l),
              precision_rows(dialect_draws(mod11$cons), "Consistency within day × dialect", bd_l))
kable(prec, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Slopes through time (SD per SD of date), the change they imply over the whole season, the posterior probability that the slope is negligible (|slope| < 0.1) and the approximate minimum detectable slope")
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

#### Summary

```{r precision summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| echo: false

for (m in unique(prec$Measure)) {
    r <- prec[prec$Measure == m, ]
    cat("- ", m, ": ", paste(sprintf("%s %s (slope %s [%s–%s], P(negligible) = %.2f, minimum detectable slope %.2f)", r$Group, tolower(r$Conclusion),
                                       f2(r$Slope), f2(r[["2.5%"]]), f2(r[["97.5%"]]), r[["P(inside ROPE)"]], r[["Minimum detectable slope"]]), collapse = "; "), "\n", sep = "")
}
```

:::

# Robustness to the hyperparameter configuration

The main results use the selected configuration of each classifier. To check that they do not depend on that choice, the same counts were obtained with each of the configurations compared in the [model fitting](birdnet_model_fitting.qmd) report: focal bellbird clips classified by the 5 fold models of each configuration (ensemble, with that configuration's out-of-fold thresholds), and other bellbirds by its out-of-fold predictions. Configurations whose training diverged were left out.

```{r robustness data}
allp <- read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "predictions_all_configurations.csv"))
allp <- allp[grepl("^R", allp$config), ] # the random-search configurations
# configurations whose training diverged (a classifier that leaves over 90% of clips unassigned,
# never reaching the 0.05 reporting limit in some folds) are left out
unassigned <- tapply(allp$predicted == "Unassigned", list(allp$config, allp$model), mean)
diverged <- rownames(unassigned)[apply(unassigned > 0.9, 1, any)]
allp <- allp[allp$true %in% c("focal", "Procnias tricarunculatus") & !allp$config %in% diverged, ]
rob_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(allp, allp$config), function(d) {
    sa <- d[d$model == "sympatric_and_allopatric", ]
    s <- d[d$model == "sympatric" & d$predicted != "Unassigned", ]
    fs <- sum(sa$true == "focal" & sa$predicted %in% heterosp_sympatric)
    fa <- sum(sa$true == "focal" & sa$predicted %in% allopatric_spp)
    data.frame(config = d$config[1],
               focal_sympatric = fs, focal_allopatric = fa, ratio = fs / fa, share = fs / (fs + fa),
               others_heterospecific = sum(sa$true != "focal" & sa$predicted %in% c(heterosp_sympatric, allopatric_spp)),
               others_total = sum(sa$true != "focal"),
               focal_model_sp = mean(s$predicted[s$true == "focal"] != "Procnias tricarunculatus"),
               others_model_sp = mean(s$predicted[s$true != "focal"] != "Procnias tricarunculatus"))
}))
rob_tab$selected <- ifelse(rob_tab$config == best_cfg[["sympatric_and_allopatric"]] & rob_tab$config == best_cfg[["sympatric"]], "both classifiers",
                    ifelse(rob_tab$config == best_cfg[["sympatric_and_allopatric"]], "sympatric + allopatric",
                    ifelse(rob_tab$config == best_cfg[["sympatric"]], "sympatric only", "")))
```

```{r robustness plot}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4

rl <- rbind(data.frame(config = rob_tab$config, panel = "Sympatric + allopatric classifier:\nfocal heterospecific classifications\nthat are the sympatric species", value = rob_tab$share, bird = "Focal bellbird"),
            data.frame(config = rob_tab$config, panel = "Sympatric-only classifier:\nassigned clips classified\nas a model species", value = rob_tab$focal_model_sp, bird = "Focal bellbird"),
            data.frame(config = rob_tab$config, panel = "Sympatric-only classifier:\nassigned clips classified\nas a model species", value = rob_tab$others_model_sp, bird = "Other bellbirds"))
rl$selected <- rl$config %in% best_cfg

ggplot(rl, aes(bird, value, color = bird)) +
    geom_hline(data = data.frame(panel = unique(rl$panel)[1], y = 0.5), aes(yintercept = y), linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_point(data = rl[rl$selected, ], shape = 21, size = 4, stroke = 1.2, color = "black") +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`Focal bellbird` = "#E07B39", `Other bellbirds` = "#408AB4"), guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank())
```

Each point is one configuration; circled: selected configurations. Dashed line: equal classification as sympatric and allopatric species, expected by chance.

```{r robustness table}
rt <- rob_tab[order(-rob_tab$ratio), ]
kable(data.frame(Configuration = rt$config, Selected = rt$selected,
                 `Focal: sympatric vs allopatric` = paste(rt$focal_sympatric, "vs", rt$focal_allopatric),
                 `Sympatric : allopatric` = round(rt$ratio, 1),
                 `Other bellbirds classified as heterospecific` = paste(rt$others_heterospecific, "of", rt$others_total),
                 `Focal classified as model species (sympatric only)` = scales::percent(rt$focal_model_sp, 0.1),
                 `Others classified as model species (sympatric only)` = scales::percent(rt$others_model_sp, 0.1),
                 check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

#### Summary

- Across the `r nrow(rob_tab)` hyperparameter configurations whose training converged (`r paste(diverged, collapse = ", ")` diverged and left almost every clip unassigned), `r round(100 * min(rob_tab$share))`–`r round(100 * max(rob_tab$share))`% of the heterospecific classifications of the focal bellbird were the sympatric species (sympatric : allopatric `r round(min(rob_tab$ratio), 1)`–`r round(max(rob_tab$ratio), 1)` : 1), and other bellbirds were classified as a heterospecific in at most `r max(rob_tab$others_heterospecific)` of `r rob_tab$others_total[1]` clips
- With the sympatric-only classifier, `r round(100 * min(rob_tab$focal_model_sp))`–`r round(100 * max(rob_tab$focal_model_sp))`% of the assigned focal bellbird clips were classified as a model species, against at most `r round(100 * max(rob_tab$others_model_sp), 1)`% of other bellbird clips. The conclusions do not depend on the configuration chosen

:::
